title: Inserzoni
body:
Now in its third edition, Inserzioni confirms its role as a permanent laboratory at Castello di Rivoli. Conceived to invite contemporary artists to engage with the unfinished architecture of the Castle and with the Collection display, the project periodically transforms the Museum’s Collection displays into an ever-evolving exhibition. Curated by Francesco Manacorda (from September 25, 2026), the program of commissions at Castello di Rivoli invites artists to create new works in dialogue with the Castle’s spaces and with the permanent Collection.

In an era in which monuments and urban spaces have increasingly become a place of contested historical assessment – driven by identity dynamics as well as migratory phenomena and other agents of division – creative thought engages with one of the urgencies that is increasingly emerging in different societies: finding an answer to the question, “Where do you live?”

Created to transform the museum into a place of production as well as preservation, Inserzioni periodically alters the exhibition route through interventions that take shape from the spaces of the Castle. The new works do not simply occupy the Museum’s galleries, but establish relationships with their history, their original function, and the works in the Collection, altering the way these spaces are traversed and understood.

The commission by Sung Tieu (Hải Dương, Vietnam, 1987) forms part of the research the artist developed for the German Pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale Arte, where the exhibition Ruin transformed the architecture that has housed Germany’s participation in the Giardini since 1905 into a modernist ruin by covering its façade with millions of mosaic tiles inspired by the Plattenbauten, the prefabricated buildings of East Germany intended, among others, for so-called “contract workers,” many of whom came from Vietnam.

This research takes on a new dimension in Room 18 of Castello di Rivoli, which is accessed through a corridor conceived as a transit space. An environment clad in mosaics introduces visitors to an installation composed of photographs, architectural fragments from a demolished building, and monochromatic light inspired by the lighting of German Autobahns, which radically alters the perception of color. Through elements belonging both to personal memory and to urban history, Tieu constructs an experience in which architecture becomes the place where dynamics of control, marginalisation, and belonging are manifested. The exhibition space is not merely a container for the work, but a perceptual device that makes visible the often invisible forms through which contemporary society determines who can inhabit a place, under what conditions, and according to which power relations.

With this third edition, Inserzioni confirms Castello di Rivoli’s role as a place where contemporary commissions become an integral part of the life of the museum. If the Collection preserves the history of contemporary art, the new commissions extend its narrative, making the Castle a space in which the present continues to be shaped through the artists’ practice.
